text:
support-erin: Customer (acme-inc) reporting lots of 504s this morning, increasing P95 tail timeouts on hosted API. They see timeouts around 15-20s. Impacting batch jobs and realtime docs.
oncall-tyler: putting oncall now, can you paste a sample request id or curl? also: @sre-jamie fyi
support-erin: sample curl and response header from acme:
```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***' -d '{"input":"long document..."}' https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate
< HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
< x-request-id: r-abc123
< x-queue-depth: 512
```
They also forwarded a client trace: tail latency spikes then 504.
sre-jamie: seeing matching alerts: ingress.queue.depth > 480 on hosted-cluster-eu-west-1 around 07:12 UTC. Continuous-batcher backlog growth observed. TAG: cbatch-queue-slab
eng-runtime-liu: likely continuous batching backlog + KV cache spinup. If queue depth passes batcher limit, requests get deferred and hit a backend deadline. Any logs with batcher backlog size?
support-erin: user sent a heap of long-seq (seq_len ~ 2048) requests in a short window; they were doing a migration. They gave some internal server log snippets:
```
[07:11:58] batcher: pending=620 inflight=12 max_depth=600
[07:12:03] kvcache: miss_rate=0.92 spinup_ms=4200
[07:12:05] dequeue: took=150ms backlog=430
[07:12:10] request r-abc123 timed out after 20000ms
```
oncall-tyler: oof. backlog > max_depth, queue spilling. Short term: enable early-shed policy for that tenant or bump queue max_depth? What's the customer tier? cs-ramirez?
cs-ramirez: acme-inc is mid-enterprise on dedicated billing but hosted runtime. We can apply tenant-level soft limits; need SRE to confirm safe ops.
sre-jamie: safe mitigation: 1) enable tenant early-reject (reject when queue > 450) 2) lower continuous-batch window to 10ms for that shard 3) temporally scale up pool by +2 GPUs on eu-west-1. I'll run steps 1 and 2 now, tagging ops.
eng-runtime-liu: also suggest lowering per-request max_seq for batching (cap at 1024) to reduce KV cache spin time. We should avoid full max_depth bump unless capacity added.
deploy-bot: deploy triggered: ops/queue-early-reject -> staged on hosted-cluster-eu-west-1 (runbook: runbook/queue-spillback)
oncall-tyler: after early-reject flip, monitoring... watch p95 and 504 rate.
sre-jamie: immediate results: 504 rate dropped ~60%, queue depth stabilized around 320. Customer still seeing occasional 504s during their large migration bursts.
support-erin: shared mitigations and repro steps with acme: throttle their migration to 20 qps, or run in batches of 50 smaller docs instead of single huge requests.
cs-ramirez: Customer accepted temporary throttle. They're asking for root cause writeup and long-term fix.
eng-runtime-liu: root cause summary proposal: 1) unthrottled long-seq traffic created KV cache cold starts + large batch assembly time -> increased per-request processing time. 2) Continuous-batcher kept accumulating requests until queue depth exceeded configured max_depth -> early dequeue stalls and deadline expirations (20s). 3) Lack of tenant-level early-shed policy allowed tenant to monopolize shard capacity.
sre-jamie: long-term fixes: tenant rate-limit (burst-aware), dynamic batch-window shrink when backlog > X, fast-path for requests that miss KV cache to avoid holding queue slot, and improved autoscale runbook for rapid short bursts.
oncall-tyler: adding checklist for postmortem: timestamps, request-ids, config values (max_depth, batch_window_ms), mitigation timeline, and customer comms.
support-erin: I've sent a short status update to acme and scheduled a follow-up call. They want an ETA for long-term changes.
eng-runtime-liu: estimating prototyping dynamic batch-window and fast-path will take 2-3 sprints; we can prioritize a patch to cap max per-request seq in batching logic this sprint.
cs-ramirez: I'll communicate that to the customer and offer a temporary dedicated capacity trial while fixes are implemented.
sre-jamie: closing ops loop: re-enabled normal defaults at 08:30 after migration throttled. Will prepare postmortem doc.
support-erin: thanks team :thumbsup: will attach logs and the customer's repro script to the postmortem.
